192.label: Owl-like face and frontal eyes
192.observation: The four inspected owl photos show prominent forward-facing eyes, broad heads and relatively short central bills. Plumage and ear tufts differ; ear tufts are not shared by all four.
192.hypothesis: This feature may associate with owl head/face structure.
192.alternative: It may primarily encode the family Strigidae or the complete owl appearance, rather than an independently controllable face trait.
192.future_test: Hold species, prompt and seed fixed; change feature 192 and check face/eye structure while measuring unintended changes in plumage, body and background. Include non-owl controls.

190.label: Long pointed bill in kingfishers
190.observation: All four kingfisher photos show an elongated pointed bill, despite substantial differences in color and markings. The Pied Kingfisher's bill is open, so pose differs.
190.hypothesis: This feature may associate with the elongated bill and head proportions typical of kingfishers.
190.alternative: All top-eight training examples are Alcedinidae; family wording and overall kingfisher identity are confounded with bill shape.
190.future_test: Measure bill length relative to head size under small feature edits across several species and seeds; check whether the entire animal changes into a kingfisher.

208.label: Rounded, domed ladybird body
208.observation: The four ladybird references show compact oval or rounded bodies and curved wing covers. Color and spots vary; the spotless example rules out treating this simply as a spots feature.
208.hypothesis: This feature may associate with rounded body/wing-cover shape.
208.alternative: It may encode Coccinellidae identity or beetle appearance broadly. One small reference shows limited detail, and there are no controlled shape measurements.
208.future_test: Vary feature 208 while tracking body outline and wing-cover curvature; use spotted and spotless examples and inspect unwanted color changes.

598.label: Squirrel-like fur and bushy tail
598.observation: All four squirrel photos show fur and small rounded or pointed ears; several clearly show a bushy tail, while the tail is only partly visible in the Pallas's squirrel view. Ear tufts and body markings vary.
598.hypothesis: This feature may associate with squirrel-like body and tail appearance.
598.alternative: It may encode Sciuridae identity; the selected photos cannot isolate tail bushiness from the rest of the animal.
598.future_test: Use full-body generations with visible tails; measure whether tail fullness changes without changing species, pose, fur color or body size.

287.label: Radial tentacles in sea anemones
287.observation: The four anemone photographs show tentacles arranged around a central disc. Their colors, tentacle proportions and body surfaces differ substantially.
287.hypothesis: This feature may associate with radial tentacle organization.
287.alternative: It may encode sea-anemone taxonomy or the whole body plan. All four displayed photos are Actiniidae, although the top-eight list also includes Sagartiidae.
287.future_test: Vary feature 287 while inspecting tentacle arrangement and count across different anemones; check whether it instead changes the whole organism or scene.
